paragraphs.text: Every morning, Anna wakes up at seven o'clock. She goes to the kitchen and makes coffee. The coffee is hot and smells good.

highlightedWords.definition: stops sleeping and opens her eyes
the room where you cook food

paragraphs.text: Anna sits at the table. She drinks her coffee slowly and reads the news on her phone. It is a quiet morning.

highlightedWords.definition: not fast, taking a lot of time
with little noise, calm

paragraphs.text: Her cat, Milo, jumps on the table. Anna laughs and gives Milo some milk. They are both happy.

highlightedWords.definition: moves up quickly with the legs
makes a happy sound when something is funny

paragraphs.text: At eight o'clock, Anna gets dressed and leaves the house. She walks to work. The morning is sunny and warm.

highlightedWords.definition: puts on clothes
bright with sunlight

paragraphs.text: Sofia arrived in London for the first time. She was excited but also a little nervous. She had a map and a list of places she wanted to visit.

highlightedWords.definition: reached a place after travelling
worried and a little afraid

paragraphs.text: On her first morning, Sofia took the Underground to get to the city centre. She got confused and took the wrong train. She ended up in East London instead of Westminster.

highlightedWords.definition: the London metro system
unable to understand or think clearly

paragraphs.text: A friendly local noticed she looked lost. He explained the route and showed her which line to take. Sofia thanked him and got back on the right train.

highlightedWords.definition: a person who lives in that area
the path you take to reach a place

paragraphs.text: By noon, Sofia was standing in front of Big Ben. She smiled and took a photo. Getting lost had taken extra time, but she had also discovered a lovely street market along the way.

highlightedWords.definition: found something for the first time
a place where people buy and sell things

questions.question: Why did Sofia end up in East London?
Who helped Sofia find the right route?
What positive thing happened because Sofia got lost?

paragraphs.text: Marcus had been applying for jobs for three months when he finally received an interview invitation from a marketing agency. He was thrilled, but also terrified. His last interview had gone terribly wrong.

highlightedWords.definition: formally requesting a job or position
extremely frightened

paragraphs.text: This time, he decided to prepare thoroughly. He researched the company, practised common interview questions in front of a mirror, and even asked a friend to do a mock interview with him.

highlightedWords.definition: completely and with great attention to detail
done for practice, not for real

paragraphs.text: On the day of the interview, Marcus dressed smartly and arrived ten minutes early. He greeted the receptionist warmly and took a few deep breaths while waiting. When his name was called, he walked in with a confident smile.

highlightedWords.definition: a person who greets visitors at a front desk
feeling sure about yourself

paragraphs.text: The interview lasted forty-five minutes. Marcus answered every question clearly and gave specific examples from his past experience. At the end, the interviewer said, 'We'll be in touch.' Three days later, Marcus got the job offer.

highlightedWords.definition: clear and detailed, not vague
a formal proposal to give someone something

What did Marcus do to prepare for the interview?
options: He read a book about marketing
He researched the company and practised with a friend
He called the interviewer in advance

paragraphs.text: When Yuki moved from Tokyo to Berlin, she anticipated a period of adjustment. What she hadn't expected was how profoundly the experience would challenge her sense of identity. In Japan, blending in was a virtue; in Berlin, standing out was celebrated.

highlightedWords.definition: expected something to happen
in a deep and significant way

paragraphs.text: The directness of Germans initially struck her as rude. Colleagues gave blunt feedback in meetings without sugarcoating their opinions. It took Yuki several weeks to realise that this was not hostility — it was simply a different cultural framework for honesty.

highlightedWords.definition: very direct and honest, sometimes to the point of being impolite
making something unpleasant seem nicer than it is

paragraphs.text: Over time, Yuki developed what psychologists call a 'bicultural identity' — she no longer felt compelled to choose between her Japanese roots and her new European life. She began to see the world through two cultural lenses simultaneously, which made her more empathetic and adaptable.

highlightedWords.definition: forced to do something
able to understand and share other people's feelings

paragraphs.text: Two years later, Yuki was offered a role leading cross-cultural projects at her company. Her manager told her that her unique perspective was invaluable. What had once felt like a personal struggle had become her greatest professional asset.

highlightedWords.definition: extremely useful, beyond price
a valuable quality or skill

questions.question: What cultural difference surprised Yuki most about Germany?
What is a 'bicultural identity' as described in the story?
options: Feeling comfortable with two cultural frameworks
Working in two countries at once

questions.question: How did Yuki's experience abroad affect her career?
options: She was offered a role in cross-cultural projects
